title: NIV for COPD exacerbation
stem: Resus 4. Mr Tse, 70, with known COPD, has been increasingly breathless for 3 days. On 28% oxygen: HR 110, BP 150/90, RR 30, SpO2 90%. Arterial gas: pH 7.26, PaCO2 9.1 kPa, PaO2 7.9 kPa, HCO3 30. He is alert. Start non-invasive ventilation.

phases.title: Medical therapy
phases.goal: Monitoring, controlled oxygen, and optimal medical therapy from the cart.

phases.title: Decide
phases.goal: Does he meet the criteria for NIV? Any contraindication? What is his ceiling of care?

phases.title: Set up NIV
phases.goal: Explain it to him, then set up the machine yourself.

phases.title: Titrate
phases.goal: Titrate the pressure and check the gas.

review.text: High-flow nasal oxygen. Your notes list NIV and HFNO side by side. HFNO is not a substitute for NIV in acute hypercapnic acidosis (pH under 7.35, PaCO2 over 6.5 kPa); start NIV within 60 minutes of the gas that shows the need.

notes:
Checked against BTS/ICS guideline on acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (2016), BTS quality standards for NIV (2018) and GOLD 2025.

Indication: acute hypercapnic respiratory failure — pH under 7.35 and PaCO2 over 6.5 kPa — persisting despite optimal medical therapy (controlled oxygen to 88–92%, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, steroids, antibiotics if indicated). Start within 60 minutes of the gas that shows the need (BTS). Contraindications: undrained pneumothorax, inability to protect the airway, vomiting, recent upper GI surgery, facial trauma or burns, fixed upper airway obstruction; decide a ceiling of treatment (is he for intubation if NIV fails?).

Settings: full face mask; IPAP start 15 cmH2O, titrate up to 20 (to 25–30 if needed) over 10–30 minutes; EPAP 3–5 cmH2O; backup rate; oxygen entrained to 88–92%. Recheck gas at 1 hour (and 4 hours): worsening pH/CO2 → escalate (intubation if appropriate). Your notes list NIV and HFNO as topics; HFNO is not a substitute for NIV in hypercapnic acidosis.

Perfect script checked against BTS/ICS 2016, GOLD 2025, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (high-flow oxygen, oxygen-driven nebulisers, a tenfold steroid dose, starting IPAP at 30). Added: the chest X-ray before NIV, the indication named, and escalation if it fails.

script.say: Hello Mr Tse, I'm the emergency doctor. Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2. A chest X-ray, please: I need to exclude a pneumothorax before NIV.
Controlled oxygen: a 28% Venturi, target SpO2 88 to 92%.
Salbutamol 5 mg and ipratropium 500 micrograms, air-driven. Prednisolone 40 mg for 5 days. Amoxicillin for the purulent sputum: antibiotics.

Despite optimal therapy he's still acidotic: pH 7.26, PaCO2 9.1: acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Start NIV within the hour. No contraindication: no pneumothorax on the film, he's protecting his airway, not vomiting, no facial trauma. Ceiling of care: he's for intubation if NIV fails; that's documented.
Mr Tse, this mask fits tightly and pushes air in to help your breathing. It feels strange at first. If you're distressed, raise your hand.
